results.title: 😸 Describe a game, build it in minutes | Product Hunt
results.content:
"Make this Get started button bigger… no, not the one in the top bar, the second one, in the Team card." That's Jay describing the sentence he kept typing. He has twin girls now and no spare hours, and most of his day was going into explaining his own screen to an agent. Cakie, free while it's in beta, records the screen like a Loom while you talk over it and point at things. A minute of footage is thousands of frames, so it reads the transcript to work out which few you were actually gesturing at, then hands you those screenshots and your words as a single prompt. [...] Describe a game, pick a genre, and Playground builds you something playable in the browser in a few minutes. Then you keep going: ask it to change a rule, swap a character, turn the gravity down, and it rebuilds around the change. That second part is the hard bit, because a lot of tools can make a game from a sentence and then fall apart the moment you edit one. Google has not said whether an edit keeps your save state or starts the game over. Playing is free, generating costs weekly tokens, and it is US only for now, so there's the catch. Unity Spark is coming in a later update to handle proper 3D. [...] (sponsored)

Phonable replaces the voicemail your carrier gives you, and setup is a carrier forward that takes about a minute with your number staying yours. Someone calls, you miss it, they get a text, whether or not they leave a message. If they do leave one it arrives as text with a summary on top, so you never sit through ninety seconds to find out it was the dentist. Which is the right way round, given Sky's research found 26% of 18 to 24-year-olds actively ignore calls and 57% blank their own parents. Frits built modes for Workday, Driving, Gym and Weekend that change the greeting on a tap.
